Rationale: Well-defined NHANES cross-sectional cohort with a fully enumerated eligibility/exclusion cascade (Methods Sec. 2, Figure 1). Appropriate source population for the prediction question. The one inherent constraint -- a cross-sectional design cannot support causal claims -- is explicitly acknowledged (Methods Sec. 1, 10) rather than glossed over.

All predictors pre-specified from the literature before model building; no data-driven selection (Methods Sec. 4, with an explicit methodological argument against stepwise/LASSO selection on a fixed dataset). Consistently defined and measured across all participants. One moderate concern: current-smoking-intensity has 55.3% missingness from a genuine skip pattern, handled with imputation plus a missingness indicator and reported as such rather than hidden.

The outcome (harmonized MetS) is objectively built from lab values and treatment flags with an unusually thorough definition (Methods Sec. 3). The concern is not measurement quality but definitional sensitivity: the substituting-definition sensitivity analysis (Results Sec. 5, Table S7) shows the outcome-definition choice moves discrimination by 0.029-0.034 AUROC units -- the largest swing of the four sensitivity arms -- meaning a materially different, defensible outcome definition would have produced a different headline number. This is disclosed, not hidden, which is itself good practice, but it is a real source of between-definition variability.

Leakage-safe pipeline (single fitted-per-fold object, Methods Sec. 6), appropriate internal cross-validation and a held-out test partition are all low-risk practices. The residual concern, explicitly self-flagged in Methods Sec. 10, is that this is internal validation on a SINGLE random split under ONE fixed seed, with no external or temporal validation -- split-to-split variability is not captured by within-partition bootstrapping. 07_Q1_Rigor_Additions/code/06_temporal_validation.py now provides a genuine forward-in-time check (AUROC 0.857 to 0.840 from random-split to temporal-holdout, well-calibrated in both), which moves this domain from what would otherwise be a clean 'some concerns' toward the low end of it -- but a single temporal split is still not the same as true external validation on an independent cohort.
